summary: The agent implemented nearly all configurable collection behavior and preserved the full baseline suite, but failed the two new stream object-factory precedence cases because configured stream construction bypasses an applicable object factory.
quick_failure_summary: Stream-to-collection mappings use the configured implementation instead of the applicable object factory.

details.reasoning: Structured JUnit results show 3641/3641 baseline tests passing and 51/53 new tests passing. Both new failures are parameterizations of shouldGiveObjectFactoriesPrecedenceForStreams: the result is ChosenList rather than FactoryList. The agent correctly wired object factories into direct collection-property copies, but did not update StreamMappingMethod.ftl. Its unchanged immediate-return path therefore collects directly into the configured implementation instead of first materializing through the factory-backed IterableCreation path.
details.secondary_factors: The agent added a configured-stream test but did not test the explicitly required combination of a configured implementation and an applicable object factory for a stream result; its final report nevertheless claimed object-factory precedence was covered.

justification.issue_description: Applicable object factories do not take precedence over configured implementations for collection results materialized from streams.
justification.evidence: The prompt explicitly says the rule applies to collection results materialized from streams and that 'an applicable object factory still wins.' The visible StreamMappingMethod.ftl immediate-return condition ignores factoryMethod, while IterableCreation already carries mappingMethod.getFactoryMethod(), making the needed integration point inferable from production code. The reference solution fixes exactly those template conditions. The hidden test merely exercises the already-stated requirement.
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT rather than a test mismatch or undocumented edge case because the failed behavior is stated directly and unambiguously in the task. The implementation is otherwise complete and runnable, so the dominant defect is omission of one explicit mapping-form interaction.

problem_assessment.notes: The prompt is detailed and explicitly covers streams, direct property copies, later processing rounds, constructor validation, and object-factory precedence. The failing expectation is deterministic and directly specified. The task is broad and appropriately challenging but demonstrably solvable by the reference patch.

evidence: The verifier successfully executed all 3641 baseline nodes and 53 new-test nodes; only two assertion failures occurred in the agent-modified behavior.

The post-agent log reports an initial 3-way test.patch merge failure, then resets the affected files, reapplies the harness, and proceeds to a complete test run, so the merge issue did not block evaluation.

The trajectory contains minor recoverable friction, including permission noise from an overly broad find and a transient patch-helper issue, but the agent continued, completed the implementation, and reported its own processor suite and style checks green.

Both failures consistently report FactoryList expected but ChosenList returned, directly matching the missing StreamMappingMethod.ftl integration rather than a bootstrap, dependency, runtime, or shared-helper failure.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker was found; the verifier reached and deterministically exposed a missing stream factory-precedence path in the implementation.
